findings.finding: The legal-effect component and participant instructions omit four distinct adopted stop situations: refusal/nonresponse within the holder published period; job/licence/housing harm and possible claim deadlines; immigration concerns and preserving underlying records; federal/out-of-state holders. Generic disputed-legal-basis wording does not cover these.

requiredStopConditions: The agency refuses to act, or does not respond within the time it publishes for records requests.
The agency asserts the expunction did not occur, or that the case is outside G.S. 15A-146(a4).
The stale record has already cost the participant a job, a licence or housing, where a claim may exist and time limits may run.
Any immigration matter, where the underlying records may be needed and this correspondence should not go out without advice.
The holder is a federal agency or an out-of-state agency, which North Carolina expunction does not reach.
requiredHandoff: If the holder refuses or does not respond, self-help ends. A second letter is not the answer and the participant needs a lawyer.

findings.repair: Add all four precise stop/referral instructions to the existing legal-effect component and participant instructions. Preserve that refusal or nonresponse ends self-help and a second letter is not the answer; obtain legal help. Preserve existing mismatch, timing, court-relief and contested-basis stops.
